# NOTES: "Out of the Blue" by Bertrand W. Sinclair (Gutenberg #73542; Blue Book Magazine, July 7, 1927)

Single book, no BOOK headings. Chapters I–XVI.

## Setting and frame
- Era: 1880s-ish cattle drive. Texas (Fort Worth, Trinity River) to Montana (Marias River, Fort Benton, Judith Basin, Sweet Grass Hills, Canada line). Longhorns, quicksand river crossings, Nebraska.
- Hero: **Rock Holloway**, young Texan range rider, tall (over medium height, towers over Kerr), keen eyes, gray Stetson, buckskin gloves, silver-inlaid gear, educated back East (father Steve Holloway; college abandoned). Rides sorrel horse **Sangre** (white star on forehead noted later; also "red horse"). Black pony carries his bed. Carries Colt .45, carbine/rifle.
- Family: mother; sister **Cecilia "Cissy"**, 17, to marry a Brett (son of Brett of the B X near El Paso). Cousin **Ben Holloway** (Ragged H, Milk River). Uncle **Tom Holloway**, captain of Rangers ("Long Tom"). Father Steve Holloway, former U.S. marshal at Abilene.

## Ch. I: A Retaining Fee (Fort Worth, April)
- **Uncle Bill Sayre**: president/manager/chief stockholder of **The Trinity Bank** (Fort Worth), tall thin-faced, age ~60, speaks dialect ("yo'", "fo'", "no'th"). Other bank men: **Marcus Proud**, **Abel Stewart**. Someone chalked "Holy" on the door (red chalk).
- Sayre's account: **Dave Snell** (dead), owned **Maltese Cross** outfit (Snell range on west fork of Trinity; ~30,000 cattle; moved to Montana). Heirs: daughter **Alice** (just 21), son (16, to be 25 before full control). Estate run as going concern; income paid annually; equal division at end.
- Executors: Sayre and **Buck Walters** (range boss; "young, ambitious, high-handed with men, powerful fond of women," dresses flash, loves stiff poker, drawn big wages ten years, never held a dollar). Sayre distrusts him.
- Dave Snell's old friend. Sayre asks Rock to go to Montana and watch Walters, "keep cases" on Maltese Cross, not as detective. Sayre gives **$500 advance in gold** (canvas bag), **$60/month** wage; "retaining fee." Rock may draw on bank in his own name; telegraph available via railroad in southern Montana.
- Rock's sorrel Sangre; Rock to ride with **Seventy Seven** trail herd (boss **Elmer Duffy**). Duffy brothers: **Joe** (noisy, harmless), **Elmer** (trail boss, tenacious, brooding, most dangerous), **Ed** (tough), **Mark** (big, bully, "as big as a house," hates Rock; "Big" Duffy).
- Seventy Seven herd bound for Marias per Sayre (not Musselshell). Joe Duffy on trail too with a Panhandle herd.
- Rock, outside town, by Trinity: "Well, Sangre..."

## Ch. II: In the Odeon (Clark's Ford, Nebraska, July)
- Clark's Ford, Platte-like Nebraska river crossing named for Ben Clark. Saloon/dance hall **the Odeon**.
- **Al Kerr**: little Texan cowman from Waco, ~5'4", gnomelike, merry blue eyes, thin hair, never killed anyone, never carried six-shooter in town; handy with rifle; 50 riders, cattle in three States. Locating in **Judith Basin, Arrow Creek**; brand **Capital K**; post office Lewistown.
- Mark Duffy enters drunk, drinks a stranger's whisky, bullies room. Lifts Kerr onto bar, shakes him, makes him buy drinks or dance; fires shot into floor. Rock steps in: "Don't be a damn fool." Duffy draws; Rock shoots him dead (Duffy's bullet passes Rock's face). Kerr's Capital K riders escort them out.
- Rock turns off three miles out. Had two months wages due; Seventy Seven is Mark's brother's outfit—feud risk.

## Ch. III: The Steering Wheel (trail north, summer–winter, Canada)
- Rock rides alone; passes a Maltese Cross herd (camped, trail boss said nothing).
- Joins short-handed **Steering Wheel** trail herd (1200 cattle, 8 men) bound for Old Man River near Fort MacLeod, Canada. Brand: steering wheel on left ribs. Crossed Missouri where Chief Joseph forded (Missouri crossing).
- Winter at Steering Wheel ranch (Canada). Boss **Dave Wells**: tall, thin-faced, drawly Texan, reticent ("sho'", "yo'"). Rock suspects odd: 1200 cattle, nine riders idle.
- April: Wells sends 4 men off; organizes horse gathering; returns 3 weeks later with 5 men and 40 horses (ridden to standstill). Discharges four riders; they find "doggies" (actually longhorns with fresh Steering Wheel brand, no other brands). Rock's suspicions.
- Red-headed youth **Billy Gore** (no, Billy Gore asked deputy foreman; deputy foreman red-headed).
- Rock parts from the Steering Wheel riders under the Sweet Grass Hills; heads toward Fort Benton in June.

## Ch. IV: A Dead Double (Marias valley)
- Rock works as mule packer for cavalry near Milk River / Fort Assiniboine (5 days, $5/day, $25 total).
- Finds TL ranch on Marias (7 miles above Maltese Cross on lower Marias; Seventy Seven ~same distance above). Stable: two saddled horses; one saddle bloodstained.
- Woman **Nona Parke**: ~20–21, dark hair, deep-gray eyes "like pools," scarlet lips, slender, imperious, deep throaty voice, educated (clean enunciation). Daughter of **Mr. Parke** (came 4 years ago with ~9000 cattle, drove 3 trail herds from Pecos; lost most in severe winter; father injured by horse fall, died). Mother died at Betty's birth.
- Child **Betty**, ~3 (yellow-haired, blue eyes), calls Rock "Doc," rag doll.
- Dead man: **Doc Martin**, TL rider, shot once in chest ~30 min earlier; ambushed while riding river bottoms with Nona up the river ("around the bend"). Looked identical to Rock. Rock also called Doc's identity; Rock said "Rock Holloway."
- Rock sleeps by stable under stars; Orion's belt.

## Ch. V: Wrapped in Canvas
- Parke graves: mother, father (horse fell on dad), and now Doc, under cottonwood, picket inclosure, 100 yds east of house.
- Body wrapped in canvas; Rock helps bury; Nona kneels praying.
- Nona: Betty first white child born north of Missouri in the Territory (per Nona). Montana: no organized county yet; U.S. marshal at Fort Benton; judge once a year.

## Ch. VI: Very Adroit Rock
- Nona hires Rock as rider at $50/month (Doc's job; $10 more than Doc?). Doc was fired once, rehired, jealous of Nona; had threatened Elmer Duffy to stay off ranch.
- Elmer Duffy arrives; mistakes Rock for Doc Martin. Rock plays along ("Hellow, Doc"); Duffy: "if I want you, I'll take you with an even break... I'm no bushwhacker." Rock says Elmer's words "I'll shoot with you" — Duffy agrees not to pursue. Rock says he'll stay out of Nona's business ("she's free agent").
- Nona: "Adroit." Rock keeps Doc identity for now.
- Half-breed nurse girl **Mary Vieux** (lives down river; Vieux family), 16, moon-faced, dark-haired.
- Ride: Nona shows him TL cattle; "TL brand, left rib."

## Ch. VII: Mariners
- Rock rides to White Springs; encounters TL/Maltese Cross roundup: **Charlie Shaw** (TL rider, ~20, blue eyes, white teeth, Parke rider; "Hello, Doc, old boy"); **Alice Snell** (tawny/yellow hair, black eyebrows, deep blue-purple eyes, dimple, green corduroy split skirt, hand-carved saddle, rides with Buck); **Buck Walters** (Maltese Cross range boss; large, well-dressed, agate-gray eyes, past thirty, grunts "Hello, Martin"; cold stare suggests Doc hostility).
- Alice: "Tell Nona to ride over..."; Alice's heir status: inherits Maltese Cross with brother when boy comes of age.
- Rock recalls Doc's saddle; cache plan.
- Nona: Doc's grave; Mark Duffy death revealed; Elmer hated Doc; Nona: "couldn't trust Elmer as far as I could throw a bull."
- Nona and Rock ride checking TL cattle; Nona watches herd "like a miser" – unexplained uneasiness about missing calves.
- Charlie Shaw returns with news.

## Ch. VIII: Getting Down to Cases
- Charlie: whisper Rock rustles with **Burris boys** (behind the Goosebill). Buck aims to get Rock (over Alice). Buck's crew: hard men (two killers who hang around home ranch, "Killer" look; Joe Stack, Bill Hurley later).
- Rock shows Charlie Doc's gear locked in room; reveals identity; Charlie accepts Rock as Doc's lookalike.
- Nona has calf count short ~70–80. Charlie says Alice loved Doc; Buck jealous; Alice said she'd can Buck but father made him administrator.
- Nona: hay; Rock to Fort Benton to hire two haying men.

## Ch. IX: Ordered South
- Fort Benton description: former Northwest Fur Co. post; Grand Union Hotel; Bear Paws; Goosebill visible.
- Rock sees **Buck Walters and Dave Wells** together at bar. Rock tells Wells he's "Doc"/denial; Wells says "Rock Holloway, darn you!" Walters: "His name is Doc Martin."
- Hires two men (only two needy). At night on street: Walters threatens Rock: "This country ain't healthy for you... go South." "Second time I've warned you... I will shut your mouth for good, inside of forty-eight hours." Walters: "my friend Dave Wells will kill you before you get it out." Rock nearly slaps Walters; holds back.
- Walters admits "a cinch... on me... and on the Maltese Cross"; "too much at stake."

## Ch. X: Thirty Angry Men
- Next morning Alice Snell gallops to TL: Walters and Elmer Duffy with boys coming to hang Doc for stealing cattle. Rock prepares; arms himself with carbine; Nona and Alice on porch.
- ~30 riders: Walters, Elmer Duffy, Charlie Shaw riding with them.
- Rock: "I am not Doc Martin." Nona backs him: "That is a lie." Charlie says so too. Charlie slipped inside with two guns.
- Elmer: "If you ain't Doc Martin, there's only one other man you could be." Rock names himself: Rock Holloway; points to sorrel JB branded, black Bleeding Heart; Elmer says "You're Rock Holloway."
- Walters smooth; he says "Burris thieves incriminated your man Martin... we'll hang him." Walters: "I'll have to take Elmer's word for it. He ought to know you, seein' you killed his brother" (taunt).
- Alice: "Doc Martin never stole anything... You were afraid of him... I hate you."

## Ch. XI: Riders on a Rise
- Nona & Rock talk; Alice upset; Nona says Doc made love to Alice. Rock teases Nona: "You steal hearts." Rock says he might quit; Nona asks him to stay.
- Rock: county election in about a month (judge of superior court, sheriff, treasurer, clerk, commissioners).
- Charlie: Burris boys "cleaned up" last night (per boys); Charlie fine.
- Five miles from home, two riders watch from a rise. Rock goes for work horses. Ambushed in ravine: shot in head (scalp grazed). Horse shot. Rock kills one (Maltese Cross-brand horse rider). Man: **Joe Stack** (captured; hog-tied). Dead partner **Bill Hurley** (shot Doc Martin; Stack confirms).

## Ch. XII: Stack Decides to Talk
- Rock wraps head with silk handkerchief; Stack captured; Rock burns Stack's foot to make him talk. Stack admits Buck offered $500 for Rock (and Hurley shot Doc Martin).
- Rock frees Stack, gives him a Maltese Cross horse, blanket, grub, advice to head south. Stack: Buck likely gone North with hand-picked crew.
- Rock's family: Steve Holloway (U.S. marshal Abilene), Tom Holloway (ranger captain, "Long Tom"), Ben Holloway (Ragged H), others.

## Ch. XIII: On the Warpath
- Nona cleans/dresses Rock's wound (carbolic, court-plaster). Buck and half his crew took a wagon and left the morning after the hanging; hard men went.
- Rock tells Charlie: Buck's hidden corrals on Sweet Grass (branding chute, "Doc" told Charlie; Doc told Buck about rancher ambition).
- Rock pulls out at dawn. Kisses Nona (unexpected) before leaving. Rides to Fort Benton, ferry, Billings (Northern Pacific), wires Sayre.
- Judith Basin: Al Kerr's Capital K; Kerr loaned by Sayre (Sayre loaned $20,000 to Kerr). Kerr sends a dozen men.

## Ch. XIV: Hot on the Trail
- Rock wires Sayre (long message); reply: "Act on your own judgment. Will back any action you take. Suspected this. Coming north, first train. —Sayre."
- Rock travels by buggy from Billings to Kerr ranch (110 miles, 17 hours). Then north with Kerr's dozen men, chuck wagon, 100 horses; reaches Marias above Nona's upper fence.
- Charlie Shaw joins Rock at camp. Charlie: Buck and six pet snakes camped on creek five miles from corrals; five riders with pack outfits and ~40 horses joined from North.

## Ch. XV: Popping Guns
- Sweet Grass Hills: Gold Butte (middle), West Butte, East Butte (largest, northmost). Camp on East Butte.
- Hidden dumbbell-shaped corrals under bank, tucked in pines, open basin ~300–400 acres. Branding Steering Wheel over Maltese Cross on steers; cattle run through chute with running iron.
- Buck Walters and Dave Wells seen working brands; eight men in sight.
- Lookout shoots Charlie Shaw (falls over bank, wounded). Rock flees on horse; pursued; horse shot; Rock fights from behind dead horse.
- Walters charges on black horse with white face (the horse he rode to hang Doc). Rock shoots Walters at twenty yards (dies). Black horse crashes onto Rock; Rock shot horse in face. Rock struck; faints. Sees Nona's face.

## Ch. XVI: "Certainly Not Sad."
- Herd of Maltese Cross-branded cattle; Capital K horses guard; bunk house with prisoners (Maltese Cross/Steering Wheel men).
- Uncle Bill Sayre at TL. Rock tells him story. Wells and Walters dead; ~2000 cattle reworked. Steering Wheel crowd from Canada.
- Walters borrowed $25,000 a year ago winter on his coadministrator prospects, bought 1200 head in Panhandle (Steering Wheel). Sayre offers Rock running of Maltese Cross; Rock says "I'll tell you 'Yes' or 'No' to-morrow."
- Sayre: will make Nona's missing calves good ("brand a hundred for her on fall round-up").
- Rock returns to TL; Elmer Duffy there pleading with Nona to marry him. Elmer shakes Rock's hand, friendly; leaves.
- Charlie shot, sent to Benton in a wagon, "lived it out three days."
- Rock to Nona: "Darn you! Do you like me, or don't you?" Nona: "I like you a heap." Tears: "there are two times when every woman cries... when she's very happy. And I'm certainly not sad!"
